tools.name: WixREADME
tools.description:
# Tool: WixREADME
The context every other Wix tool assumes. Call it first, once per conversation, for any Wix task or question; for another site later in the conversation, call `GetSiteContext` instead of calling this again.
A Wix task includes reading or changing a site's or account's data: products, inventory, carts, checkouts, orders, bookings, services, staff, time slots, rentals, restaurant menus, online orders, reservations, events, tickets, RSVPs, blog posts, CMS collections and items, pricing plans, subscriptions, portfolios, gift cards, coupons, donations, forms, form submissions, contacts, members, loyalty points, groups, reviews, inbox messages, CRM tasks, automations, email campaigns, payments, invoices, SEO, redirects, translations, locations, analytics, media files, site properties, installed apps, and the account's sites and domains (searching whether a domain is available, buying one, and connecting one bought elsewhere).
These requests skip it and go straight to their own tool:
- **Creating a new site.** Skip the docs too. A site is written in code and uploaded: StartDeployWebsite returns the upload guide; StartHeadlessBuild returns the headless guide, for a site that needs Wix business features (a store, bookings or appointments, rentals, events and tickets, a restaurant menu with online orders or reservations, a blog, a portfolio, pricing plans and memberships, donations, Wix Forms, members and login, a CMS, payments). Call one first, before collecting the site's name, content or style: StartHeadlessBuild when the site needs Wix business features, otherwise StartDeployWebsite. Each only returns its guide, and details the user has not given are handled after it. A Studio Two (Studio 2) site, new or existing (to build, change, export or import it): StartStudioTwoSite. WixHarmonyEditorBuild or SearchSiteTemplates only when the user asked for Wix's editor, the Wix Harmony Editor, a template, Wix Studio or the Classic Editor. Never create a site through ManageWixSite, CallWixSiteAPI or ExecuteWixAPI.
- **Suggesting domain names**: call GetSuggestedDomains directly, with the business or site name as the query, and the site's siteId for a Wix site.
- **Listing, showing or finding their Wix sites**: call ListWixSites directly.
- **Uploading local or attached files (images, videos, audio, documents) to a Wix site**: call UploadImageToWixSite directly, with no docs, schema or API calls. Do NOT use ExecuteWixAPI, SearchWixAPISpec, or any Media Manager REST API for these uploads.
A question about one of those goes to the same tool ("can you show my sites?" is ListWixSites). Any other Wix question is answered from a Wix skill or the docs, never from memory; look there before answering, also when no tool seems to fit.
It returns, in full:
- **Source of truth**: nothing Wix-specific from memory. Every URL, ID, setting location, product fact, request shape and field name comes from the docs tools, a Wix skill, an earlier tool result in the conversation, or the user.
- **The site**: the account's sites with their properties and installed apps. The `siteId` comes from there (ask when several fit); a business solution's API works only on a site with its app installed, and an app's version changes its endpoints.
- **Find the method**: an earlier tool result, else a Wix skill's recipe (wix-manage to manage a site, wix-headless-kit to build a headless one), else the docs: SearchWixRESTDocumentation or BrowseWixRESTDocsMenu, then ReadFullDocsArticle; the SDK, CLI, headless and apps docs for code.
- **The exact shape**: model a call only on an example that matches the case; fill the rest with SearchWixAPISpec on the method's docs URL (request and response schemas, `method.publicUrl` for REST, `method.sdk` for the JavaScript SDK). A query's filter and sort fields and operators are a closed list per method.
- **The call, or the code**: ExecuteWixAPI runs one async function holding every step code can resolve, the reads and the writes they feed together. Code the user keeps (an app, a headless site, a script over REST or the JavaScript SDK) is written from the same shapes; the headless skills are a shortcut on that path.
- **When a call fails**: the error says what was wrong and carries a Wix request id; fix that, never resend unchanged or guess.
- **Wix skills**, what each is for and how to read one: from disk when installed (the Wix plugin, or `npx skills add wix/skills`, `--skill <name>` for one, `-g` for the user's home, into `.agents/skills/<skill>/` or a similar folder the client reads, such as `.claude/skills/<skill>/`), else online with ReadFullDocsArticle at `https://www.wix.com/skills/<skill>/<path>`.
  - **wix-manage**: REST recipes for managing a site's business solutions, one per task; follow the recipe and make its calls with ExecuteWixAPI, its docs URL in `sourceDocUrls`. Its list of recipes is `SKILL.md` in the installed skill, or online https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/articles/ai-tools/wix-mcp/skills/wix-management-recipes-index.md, and each API area has its own `<API section>/skills.md` (for example https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/bookings/skills.md).
  - **wix-headless-kit**: builds a Wix Headless site on shipped, verified code from wix-headless-templates, a `@wix/sdk` React core or the same data layer as plain REST calls: scaffold with the CLI, deploy, seed, design on the shipped hooks, release. https://www.wix.com/skills/headless-kit/SKILL.md
  - **wix-headless-templates**: the code wix-headless-kit builds from, one folder per Wix Business Solution. https://www.wix.com/skills/headless-templates/
When the user asks you to do something in Wix, do it yourself, in as few steps and questions as you can; don't tell them which docs to read or which API to call.

tools.name: ReadFullDocsArticle
tools.description:
Fetches the full Wix docs article or method article with code examples for using the method.
Docs articles looks like this: https://dev.wix.com/docs/... and they can either be general docs articles or method articles.
Also reads Wix skills pages — https://www.wix.com/skills/<skill>, https://dev.wix.com/docs/skills/<skill>, and the files they link (e.g. .../<skill>/references/<file>.md) — and Wix Headless agent pages under https://www.wix.com/headless/ (e.g. https://www.wix.com/headless/skill.md), exactly as served.
Take the URL from the user's message or an earlier tool result. To reach an article you have no URL for, search or browse the docs first.
It returns the whole file. For part of a long skills file, ExecuteWixAPI can fetch the same URL, split the text into lines and return only the lines needed ("How to read a skill" in WixREADME has the code). In ExecuteWixAPI, a dev.wix.com docs page needs `.md` added to its URL, and Help Center articles are not reachable: those are read only with this tool.
For REST docs, use the URL as-is. For SDK docs, the URL SHOULD include ?apiView=SDK.

articleUrl.description: The URL of the docs article or method article to fetch. Should be something like https://dev.wix.com/docs/.../... For REST docs, use the URL as-is. For SDK docs, the URL SHOULD include the query param ?apiView=SDK (e.g. https://dev.wix.com/docs/...?apiView=SDK). Wix Help Center articles (https://support.wix.com/en/article/...) are read as-is. Wix skills pages (https://www.wix.com/skills/..., https://dev.wix.com/docs/skills/...) and Wix Headless agent pages (https://www.wix.com/headless/..., e.g. https://www.wix.com/headless/skill.md) are read as-is, including their referenced files. Source links (https://dev.wix.com/rawdocs/api/get-source-content?repo=...&path=...) found in skills and recipes are read as-is.

tools.name: ReadFullDocsMethodSchema
tools.description:
Fetches the full method schema for a given method.
This will give you the entire request/response schema with all the fields and their descriptions.
For REST and SDK API-reference methods, prefer SearchWixAPISpec when it is available: it can fetch and inspect the exact method schema by docs URL, return the request/response shape, the JavaScript SDK call (`method.sdk`: package, namespace, method, positional parameters, examples), and inspect selected nested component schemas without dumping unrelated fields. Use ReadFullDocsMethodSchema only when SearchWixAPISpec is unavailable or did not provide the needed detail.
For REST docs, use the URL as-is. For SDK docs, the URL SHOULD include ?apiView=SDK.

articleUrl.description: The URL of the documentation to fetch. Should be something like https://dev.wix.com/docs/.../... For REST docs, use the URL as-is. For SDK docs, the URL SHOULD include the query param ?apiView=SDK (e.g. https://dev.wix.com/docs/...?apiView=SDK).

reason.description: One sentence describing the original user request, the task you are trying to accomplish, and why you need the full schema (e.g., no relevant code example found in docs or recipes).

tools.name: BrowseWixRESTDocsMenu
tools.description:
Browse the Wix REST API documentation menu hierarchy.
Alternative to SearchWixRESTDocumentation - use this to explore and discover APIs by navigating the menu structure instead of searching by keywords.
- Omit the `menuUrl` param to see top-level categories
- Pass a `menuUrl` param to drill into a category - copy the URL from previous responses
Example `menuUrl` param values for main Wix verticals:
- Stores: "https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/stores"
- Bookings: "https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/bookings"
- CMS: "https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/cms"
- CRM: "https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/crm"
- eCommerce: "https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/e-commerce"
- Events: "https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/events"
- Blog: "https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/blog"
- Pricing Plans: "https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/pricing-plans"
- Restaurants: "https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/restaurants"
- Media: "https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/assets/media"
- Site Properties: "https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-management/site-properties"

menuUrl.description: URL of the menu to browse. Empty/omitted returns the root menu. Copy the URL from links in previous responses of this tool. Example: "https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/ecommerce" or "https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/ecommerce/catalog"

reason.description: One sentence describing the original user request and why you are browsing this part of the docs menu.

tools.name: CallWixSiteAPI
tools.description:
Call apis on site "Grafika" (https://www.grafikatbilisi.com/_api/mcp). Use this to perform an action on visitor's behalf, for example, query the site's data or book an appointment.
Before calling this tool, you should ALWAYS check the rest docs (use "SearchSiteApiDocs" tool) for the specific API you want to call. The mentioned tool will give you instructions how to use the API.',
      'NEVER try to guess the API or endpoint, ALWAYS check the docs using "SearchSiteApiDocs" tool.
The url param should be taken from the "SearchSiteApiDocs" tool. It usually starts with "https://www.wixapis.com".
Authentication: when the caller sent an access token in the Authorization header, this tool uses that token and you should omit "visitorToken". Otherwise pass "visitorToken" from the GenerateVisitorToken tool.

visitorToken.description: Visitor access token. Omit it when the caller sent an access token in the Authorization header - that token is used instead. Otherwise: if you have a visitor token in your context, ALWAYS use it and do not create a new one; if you do not have one, use the GenerateVisitorToken tool to get it.

url.description: The url of the api to call - ALWAYS get the information from the API docs retrieved using the 'SearchSiteApiDocs' tool or from the conversation context, the URL MUST BE ABSOLUTE URL. Usually it starts with 'https://www.wixapis.com'.

method.description: The HTTP method to use for the API call (e.g. GET, POST, PUT, DELETE)

body.description: A string representing of a valid JSON object to describe the body of the request

tools.name: GenerateVisitorToken
tools.description:
Create a new visitor session and obtain a visitor access token for site "Grafika" (https://www.grafikatbilisi.com/_api/mcp).
You must use this tool before calling CallWixSiteAPI for this first time.
If you already have a visitor token in your context, DO NOT USE THIS TOOL AGAIN.

tools.name: SearchSiteApiDocs
tools.description:
Searches for site "Grafika" (https://www.grafikatbilisi.com/_api/mcp) API documentation and returns how to use the site using the API.
You are a helpful "Grafika" site assistant chatbot and you are helping the user perform actions on the site - to query the site's data or to perform an action on the site.
Specify the API endpoint, resource, or action you need information about (e.g., 'get site details endpoint', 'create data collection', 'update product API', 'REST authentication').
If you can't find what you need, try to rephrase your search term.
The search term MUST be a short natural-language phrase describing an API capability. Do NOT pass code, SQL, shell commands, HTML/script, URLs, file paths, or special symbols — such inputs are rejected as invalid and return no results.

searchTerm.description: A short, natural-language search term describing the API capability you need — a generic term, not too specific (e.g., "how to fetch products" instead of "avocados in stock"). Use plain words only: no code, SQL, shell commands, HTML, URLs, file paths, or special symbols.

tools.name: GetBusinessDetails
tools.description:
Get business and site details for "Grafika" (https://www.grafikatbilisi.com/_api/mcp).
This tool will return business details: timezone, phone, address, site name, business name, description, business schedule, special hour period.
It will also return site features that you can use via other tools (bookings, store, etc.).
Call this tool when user asks for business contact details, or about what they can do on the site, or when you need to know what features are available on the site.

tools.name: SearchInSite
tools.description:
Searches the site "Grafika" (https://www.grafikatbilisi.com/_api/mcp) for information.
Use this tool ONLY in the following cases:
1. You just used "GetBusinessDetails" tool and you did not find the information you need.
2. User asked a generic business question about their business (e.g., business address, business hours, contact information, return policy, etc.)
3. You already tried to find an entity (e.g., product, service, etc.) using an API tool and you did not find the information you need.
4. The request is too vague and you do not know what type of entity it is and what to search for in the docs.
Do NOT use this tool for searching for products or other offered services - use the 'SearchSiteApiDocs' tool instead (unless you already tried that tool and you did not find the information you need).
This tool DOES NOT support filters - you cannot ask questions like "find me something under $10". 
This tool searches the site's regular pages and blog posts. It does NOT cover pages generated from CMS collections (dynamic item pages). When the site has such pages, the result starts with their paths and how to list the pages under each one.

searchTerm.description: The term to search for in the site, e.g. "working hours" or "store locations"

tools.name: ExecuteWixAPI

code.description: JavaScript async function expression to execute against the Wix REST API. The value must be the function itself, for example `async function() { ... }` or `async () => { ... }`, not a script body and not an invoked function. Return the final answer from inside the function. Do not write top-level `const`, top-level `await`, or top-level `return` outside the function body. Do not import Node.js built-ins such as `fs`, `path`, or `node:*`, and do not try to write files from this code; ExecuteWixAPI only returns data from the function. Use `wix.request({ method, url, body })` for Wix API calls. Every call runs against the current visitor site; do not set `scope`, `siteId`, or auth headers. Full Wix API URLs and paths starting with `/` are supported. Wix REST API page size limits vary — use 100 as a safe default unless the method schema (via SearchWixAPISpec) confirms a higher limit is supported. For cursor-based APIs, pass the next cursor as `cursorPaging: { limit: 100, cursor: pagingMetadata.cursors.next }` — not inside `paging`. Check the method schema to confirm whether the API uses `paging` (offset-based) or `cursorPaging` (cursor-based) before paginating.

reason.description: One sentence explaining the original user request and why you are executing code to complete it.

hasMutations.description: Optional. Whether the code writes site data (create, update, delete, import, upload) or only reads it.

sourceDocUrls.description:
The URLs of the documentation, recipes, API articles, or schema sources where you confirmed the Wix REST endpoints, HTTP methods, request body shapes, auth contexts, and required fields used by this code.
Include every docs/schema source needed for the endpoints and request shapes used in the code.
The endpoints and request shapes must appear in those sources; do not guess them.
Each value must be a valid URL like:
- https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/... (REST API reference docs)
Use ["user-provided"] if the user gave you all endpoint and request details directly.
Use ["other"] only when neither applies.

files.description: Optional bundle of raw file contents for uploads, so file bytes never go through the `code` JavaScript (no escaping, no string-literal/`${}`/backtick pitfalls). Never inline file contents in `code`. Format: sections delimited by a line `=== FILE: ===` (text, raw) or `=== FILE: base64 ===` (binary, base64); `` is relative to the site root. Example: `=== FILE: index.html === === FILE: assets/app.js === console.log(1) === FILE: logo.png base64 === iVBORw0KGgo...` In `code` they are the `files` global (`{ path, content, encoding?: "base64" }[]`); `wix.multipart()` turns them into one binary-safe `multipart/form-data` body: `const mp = wix.multipart(); await wix.request({ scope: "account", method: "POST", url, headers: { "Content-Type": mp.contentType }, body: mp.body });`. Use base64 entries for small assets (icons, logos, fonts) and for files you downloaded and are re-uploading; large images/video go in by URL (``), not in the bundle. A file containing a line exactly like the delimiter is not supported.

attachments.description: A file you have (attached in the chat or created in your sandbox), passed by its file id or path. In OpenAI clients (ChatGPT, Codex) it arrives as { download_url, file_id, file_name?, mime_type? }. Other clients send the path as written, which Wix can't read; there, leave this out and use `files`, or upload from your shell if it reaches the internet. Any type: a zip of a site, HTML, images, PDFs. The bytes are fetched here and appended to the `files` global as { path, content, encoding: "base64" } entries (path = file_name), so `wix.multipart()` and `wix.unzip()` work on them unchanged. Prefer this over base64 in `files` whenever you have a file handle. Up to 10 MB per call.

visitorToken.description: Visitor access token, for an anonymous call. Omit it when you are signed in and sending your access token in the Authorization header - that token is used instead. Otherwise, if you have a visitor token in your context, ALWAYS use it and do not create a new one; if not, use the GenerateVisitorToken tool.
